measured._comment: What the original actually does, measured in DOSBox on 2026-11-12 (T-008). These are reference numbers, not the values the server runs on: `roundSeconds` and `speeds` above are a deliberate deviation for browser playability and are labelled as such in sources.speeds and notes.speeds. Evidence: docs/re/MOVEMENT.md, probe scripts in the T-008 notes directory.

pieceTable._comment: Addresses the original's per-piece pass indexes, read off the loop (decompiled.c 4381-4595) and dumped live 2026-11-12. DS-relative. The pass walks the 0..99 visit order, then indexes parallel per-unit arrays by the record number - there is no 16-byte unit record.

passRatePerRound._comment: AC3 (T-008): piece-pass wraps counted over a FULL round, not the 8 s sampler (11 wraps per 129.2 s round at speed 1, 16 at speed 3, 63-64 at speed 6; no pass at speed 0). Source: docs/re/MOVEMENT.md, AC3.

cellsPerRoundByKind._comment: AC3 table (PM 3495 item 1). Every row is keyed on the STATIC per-kind allowance byte[0x19a6 + kind] (measured.pieceTable.kindAllowance above), never on a kind identity read from 0x906 - Q35 is open. status: MEASURED = a full-round run exists and evidenceRef names it; MEASURED-HARNESS = the run exists but the harness wrote the kind nibble (PM 3481 item 2 accepts it as measuring the rule); PREDICTED = the static byte only, NO RUN: the row is (byte/20) steps per pass x the measured passes per round, a prediction and not evidence. cellsPerRound values are [low, high] cells in one 129.2 s round at that speed. Kinds 0, 3 and 4 carry a zero byte and cannot move in a pass at all; the server does not run on these numbers - move.cellsPerRound above is still the runtime table.

0.note: unused slot, zero byte; nothing moves without a budget

3.note: transport; zero byte, it moves as cargo

4.note: zero byte, no kind 4 on any checked start board

5.note: no run: predicted from byte 36; the 36-allowance band measured on kind 6 is 1.64-1.81 cells/pass, and 1.00 if the piece is land-capped at one visit per pass

7.note: no run: predicted from byte 40 (2.0 steps/pass), 1.00 if the piece is land-capped

8.note: no run: predicted from byte 40 (2.0 steps/pass), 1.00 if the piece is land-capped

9.note: no run: predicted from byte 40 (2.0 steps/pass), 1.00 if the piece is land-capped

terrain._comment: T-016: every original terrain effect in one block, each value tagged measured / disassembly / unverified with its citation. Runtime reads pathCost, crawlPace and digIn from here; attritionPerPass and shoreFire are recorded reference rows (see each entry's `wired` field). Ids are board.TERRAIN: 0 ocean, 1 docks, 2 shallows, 3 lake, 4 capital, 5 base, 6 city, 7 oilfield, 8 plain, 9 forest, 10 mountain, 11 desert, 12 jungle, 13 polar, 14 wasteland, 15 facility.

The manual's printed Slowed column (p.21) disagrees with this table; the table is the recovered fact and wins. Function: web/server/move.mjs walkLine.

crawlPace.source: Q5 MEASURED (T-016 DOSBox legs, tank kind 2, one straight corridor per terrain, pass cursor DS:0x147c, round clock DS:0x157e). Game-clock units per cell: speed 1 plain 720, forest 720, mountain 1440; speed 6 plain 122, forest 122, mountain 163 (one 2-beat cell in six). So forest is NOT slower than plain (1 beat, the archive's 2-beat stand-in was wrong for forest) and mountain is 2 beats at speed 1 and 1.33 average at speed 6. Jungle and polar keep 2 beats as UNVERIFIED because their path-cost bytes (9 and 13 of the 24-point allowance) were never walked in a leg. Transport stays the walker class rule; wasteland stays refused. Legs: docs/re/evidence/t016/q5-*.txt.

cover.source: FUN_194c_000e @ 194c:000e, decompiled.c 7039-7054: the DEFENDER's terrain byte decides cover, applied to the damage-matrix cell before flank/rear. City, capital or base: infantry kinds 1/3 lose (dmg+1)/3 and tanks (kind 2) lose dmg/5. Mountain: infantry lose dmg>>2 and tanks lose dmg/6. No attacker terrain bonus exists. This block names the id sets; the integer arithmetic lives in web/server/combat.mjs coverFor. MEASURED live (T-009b): 20 -> 13 on a city cell, 20 -> 15 on a mountain, same pairing on plain 20.

digIn.source: DS:0x1996 bit 0x20 marks a dig-in terrain: ids 7 oilfield (0xe0), 8 plain (0x60), 9 forest (0x60), 10 mountain (0x20), 11 desert (0x23), 12 jungle (0x23). decompiled.c 4523-4525 flips kind 1 to 3 on the first eligible pass (stationary, no target, bit 0x20); a move order reverts it. Not in a city or on any site terrain (their bytes carry 0x80, not 0x20).

attritionPerPass.source: DS:0x1996 low 5 bits, applied once per unit pass (FUN_1c0d_00b4, a unit is visited once per pass-cursor wrap). Q6 MEASURED live 2026-11-14 (T-016): desert 3/pass at (200,38), jungle 3/pass at (89,79), polar 5/pass at (36,10), lake 3/pass at (194,36), each one delta per pass-cursor wrap over 12 wraps from strength 100 (docs/re/evidence/t016/q6-*.txt). That closes Q6's desert contradiction: the three earlier 'flat' desert runs were taken while the round clock was 0xffff (round over, no pass), not because the terrain is inert. Wasteland stays DISASSEMBLY: the dumped byte is 31 (0x1f), the spec text says 34, and no era board contains a wasteland cell, so no leg can pin the amount or the destroy branch (a 1986 nuclear strike could create one; not feasible in a pinned single-piece probe). Site terrains (244 = 0xf4, bit 0x80) drain only a unit that does not own the site. NOT wired as the runtime rate: the remake has no pass, and the original's pass count per round is speed-dependent (measured wraps per round: ~10.6 at speed 1, ~62 at speed 6), so turning 3/pass into 3/round would be a 6-60x rate change that needs the D-017 pacing ruling; the deferral itself is recorded as decision D-024 (Decisions.md). Runtime stays on combat.attritionPerRound, a labelled per-round stand-in.
attritionPerPass.evidenceRef: docs/re/evidence/t016/q6-desert.txt, q6-jungle.txt, q6-polar.txt, q6-lake.txt, t016_q6.py; docs/re/T016_TERRAIN.md s3; config combat.measured.attritionTable

shoreFire.source: Fire beyond 2 cells caps damage at (target strength - 30); under 25 strength the shot is halved instead. DISASSEMBLY ONLY, never live-measured. WIRED in T-016 behind this block and labelled disassembly: combat.damageFor applies the cap as a floor on remaining strength, max(0, strength - 30), and halves the shot under 25. The clauses overlap at 25-30 strength: at 30 the cap is max(0, 30 - 30) = 0, so 25-30 is an immunity band. PM ruling 2026-11-14 (room 4572), interim: this reading is kept, the label stays disassembly, and the DOSBox leg is pending rather than measured. docs/re/T016_TERRAIN.md s5 records it.

spareActionBudget.source: DECODED (T-032 Part B, docs/re/AI.md 9.1-9.2): 0xe94c = 0x1a0*2 - 4, SET only under `if (1 < *(int *)0x1a0)` at decompiled.c 13231-13232 and 15157-15158, so level 1 never sets it and levels 2-5 read 0/2/4/6. Seven lines in the export touch it: 1649-1650 (the buy: decrement when nonzero, never a refusal), 3410 and 3415 (the army pass: decrement without recording the cell, or record the cell at zero), 3438 (FUN_2dfc_1874 at zero, STAND-IN) and the two setters. It is ONE counter, seeded once per game and spent in the army pass (ai_turn_process @ 107e:3bd0, 3230-3422) and by the buy, and the cell is recorded at 3411-3412 only when it is already zero, after which 3392-3400 strikes that cell out (0xf at 3398). FUN_107e_0bd6 (1126-1268) reads neither 0xe94c nor 0x1a0. The port spends it the same way: repeatPool = e94c, but that pool composes with 0bd6's pass budget rather than replacing it: 1216-1218 enters the army pass only while local_c < 3 and hands it 3 - local_c, which already carries the buy and the defence pass, and 1218 adds each dispatch back into the same counter. So in one turn the army can spend at most min(e94c, 3 - spent) repeats, and one destination cell can take at most min(1 + e94c, 3 - spent) dispatches - 1/3/3/3 at levels 2-5 with nothing else spent, fewer once the buy or a defence has acted. The pool above 2 is unreachable in one turn because the pass itself ends at three dispatches. The defence pass's ceiling is the constant 3 below, not e94c. WHEN IT IS SET: 13232 sits in FUN_20b1_01b6, the new-game setup routine (menu -> scenario 0x19e -> side 0x19c -> difficulty 0x1a0 -> map init -> return), whose ONLY caller is main_game_loop line 23; the play loop it hands off to, FUN_1000_01da(7) at 26-28, never writes the byte. The second setter line, 15158, is that same routine decompiled a second time inside the jump-table blob Ghidra labels FUN_20b1_2eea @ 20b1:2eea (size 39, warnings 15015-15048), so there is ONE setter, not two. The pool is therefore match-long: seeded 0/2/4/6 at new game for levels 2-5, never written again, spent by a repeat dispatch (3415) and by a buy (1650). The port keeps it on the match (match.botRepeatPool) and no longer resets it per turn.

bot.spareActionPassCapSource: DECODED, decompiled.c 1126-1268 (banner 1124, closing brace 1268; 1272 opens FUN_107e_0f58). FUN_107e_0bd6 keeps ONE counter, local_c, initialised at 1142 and incremented at 1188, 1192, 1195, 1199, 1209, 1213, 1218, 1222, 1226, 1244, 1247, 1251 (+3), 1254 and 1265. It is read against 3 at NINE places: 1194, 1197, 1208, 1211, 1217, 1241, 1246, 1249, 1253 (the last is a while). 1200 is `bVar2 = true`, not a read; 1202 is the exit test `(2 < local_c) || (9 < local_8)`, i.e. at most THREE successful actions and ten site visits (local_8, 1203). The combat tail takes the budget to FOUR: 1220, 1224, 1228 and 1256 test `local_c < 4`, and resolve_combat is handed `4 - local_c` (1257, 1262, 1264). The only non-counter gate in the body is era: 1207 `0x19e == 3 || 0x19e == 2` guarding FUN_107e_51b6 (1208) and FUN_107e_5500 (1211); 0x19e is the era index, not a level. The budget is level-independent: no read of 0xe94c or 0x1a0 in 1126-1268.

deviations: defaultLevel 3: a lobby request that names no level gets COL. BUCK ZEAL (3), the level the pre-T-032 bot's behaviour is compared against (T-032 Part C AC3). The original's setup always asked; nothing recovered names a default, so this is our choice, not the game's.

level 2-5 labels: presentation text, not recovered strings, and PB-264 keeps each one inside what the engine does. Level 1's label ('Stands still: practice') is fixed by T-032 B1. Level 2's pool is 0, so spendRepeat records the first destination and marchOne never re-uses it: 'never repeats a destination' is exact. Levels 3 and 4 carry the SAME string on purpose - e94c is 2 and 4, but the pool is spent one dispatch at a time across a match while 0bd6's three-action pass is rebuilt every turn, so the difference is not a per-turn promise and no label claims one. Level 5's extra clause is the PB-262 buy: decompiled.c 1632's `*(int *)0x1a0 < 5` guard means levels 2-4 re-draw from another site when the picked site's 0x10ae timer is still running and level 5 buys there anyway. The '2/4/6 spare repeats a game' wording of PM 9380 section 4 is retired by PM 9555 (AC 9537): a player reads it as six extra actions a war, which the pass cap and the pool's spend rule do not grant. The level-5 garrison gate the old labels mentioned is refused by 0x10ae (room 9370) and gone from config and code.

level 1 and 0xe94c: the original never seeds the pool at level 1 (the setter is under `if (1 < *(int *)0x1a0)`) and the setup block at 13008-13040 does not clear the byte, so a level-1 game in the original inherits whatever the previous game left. The port starts every match at 0 - stated here rather than modelled, because a served match has no previous game to inherit from.
standIns: A7 ownership counters (four counters): not read by the port. The bot reads site.owner and piece.side; STAND-IN.
A7 10-byte staging arrays (two): not modelled. Orders go straight through move.issueOrder; STAND-IN.
bot.notes: T-032 Part B. The only difficulty lever shipped is the e94c army-repeat counter, and the three-dispatch pass caps it: a pool above 2 cannot be spent in one turn (config spareActionBudget.source, docs/re/AI.md 1a). The level-5 garrison gate is REFUSED by 0x10ae, which is a once-per-round countdown, and is gone from config and code (PM ruling, room 9370). The three-action defence pass (combat tail four) is the same constant at every level (0bd6, decompiled.c 1126-1268), there is NO piece-production cap (the earlier unitCap 6 is withdrawn), and no per-level price or strength bonus exists anywhere in the bot (no rows to add - the absence is the contract). The 100-record unit table (FUN_1ac5_0008, 8105-8136) is a board bound, not a production cap: the buy refuses on a full table (1629). Opponent starting money stays the Manual p.17 spinner and is independent of the level.

loyalty.note: PB-228, TWO STAND-INS. Manual p.30: aid moves a NATION one step, hostile -> neutral -> allied; a nation with more cities takes more gifts; and "your opponent can give foreign aid to the same targets you do, thus negating your efforts". The archive printed neither the gifts-per-city count nor HOW a rival's gift cancels, so giftsPerCity (the multiplier) and counterAid (one-for-one: a gift from the other side to the same nation cancels one gift the payer had banked there, BEFORE the new gift banks) are both labelled stand-ins, not decoded values (Open RE Q52: UNVERIFIED, needs disassembly/DOSBox). counterAid false is the arms-race reading, where each side's campaign runs on its own. PB-236 THIRD STAND-IN, PORT DECISION, UNVERIFIED: announceFromCities is the size cut behind manual p.30's "only large countries make it known that they have received foreign aid". The manual prints no cut at all (no city count, no population, nothing), so 4 is a port decision, not a decoded value: the 1986 board's 30 nations carry 13, 10, 5, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2 cities and 22 of them one city each, so a cut of 4 makes USA (13), USSR (10) and Japan (5) large while China (3) and every one- or two-city nation stays quiet - the same three a cut of 5 names, because no nation on this board sits at 4. A nation AT OR ABOVE the cut announces; below it is silent. The card carries the full 30-nation census and the 2023 opening this tree ships: rolled CAPITALS, same city list: one per side, drawn per match from sites that side already owns (web/server/capitals.mjs rollCapitals; measured at 16678cd across four seeds the capital pair moves and the 62-city and 57-well owner vectors do not - 13/10/39 cities and 8/8/41 wells every time), while whether the original also rolls city and oil ownership is UNVERIFIED (B-3 unshipped, manual p.16). ONE size test covers every era: the announce cut reads the cities count carried on the aid event, so USA, USSR and Japan announce in 1986 and in 2023 alike, and 2023 is not a second rule. The clerk's alternative - the same count giftsNeeded() uses - is recorded in Open RE Q52 as the untested reading.

sources.speeds: MEASURED 2026-11-12 (T-008, docs/re/MOVEMENT.md): the original's round clock is 7646 units at 1/64 s each, i.e. 119.5 s of nominal game time, and it counts down at the same rate at every speed 0-6 (59.16 units/s in DOSBox 0.74-3 at 3000 cycles, so 129.2 s of wall clock; 3 legs per speed, 0/1/3/6). Every speed setting therefore has the SAME round length; the speed control paces piece and combat animation, not the round. Speed 0 stops piece movement dead (0 piece steps in 8 s) while the round clock still runs. DELIBERATE DEVIATION: `roundSeconds` and `speeds` above are not these numbers. They are the owner's 5 s round and 0/5/3.5/2.4/1.6/1/0.6 ramp, kept so a browser war lasts minutes rather than the original's two-hour campaign. The stand-in ordering (higher speed = shorter round) is contradicted by the original and is kept on purpose, pending a PM ruling; nothing outside this file treats it as recovered.
sources.move: cellsPerRound: STAND-IN, UNMEASURED for the per-kind numbers. Orderings only - tank > infantry and no more than 2x (p.9), ship > transport > infantry (p.21). MEASURED 2026-11-12 (T-008): the war room walks all 100 pieces in one pass and the pass rate is 7.37/s at speed 1, 12.25/s at speed 3 and 49.23/s at speed 6, with 0 steps at speed 0, so a unit under orders can advance at most one cell per pass - about 9.5, 15.8 and 63.7 cells in one 119.5 s round at speeds 1/3/6 before its per-kind budget (DS:0x6FE against DS:0x1976) throttles it. The per-kind split was NOT captured (no unit could be put under orders in the driven walk), so no per-kind number is sourced. damageMatrix._comment: DS:0x18f0, index targetKind + attackerKind*9. Row 0 overlaps the string tail 'ly = %d.' and kind 0 is an empty slot, so row 0 is never read. Dumped live 2026-11-13 and identical in CHQ_unpacked.EXE (file offset 0x341a0; the row stride 9 is confirmed against every row). This table IS the runtime: combatRules() builds it from these rows and baseDamageFor() indexes attacker*9+target; an entrenched infantry defender is looked up as kind 3 (the entrench column), not as a multiplier. Column 0 is a real byte, not padding: it is what the original reads when the TARGET is kind 9 (carrier), because a*9+9 is the next row's column 0. kindNineColumn is that row, byte for byte.
damageMatrix.runtimeWiring: attacker*9+target, kinds by name from this block's kinds map; defender kind 3 when kind === infantry && entrenched === true; target kind 9 reads kindNineColumn[attacker] (the next row's column 0); flank/rear read the attacker's facing against the defender's (same facing = rear x2, not-opposite = flank x1.5) and only while the defender is fighting a third piece.
damageMatrix.kindNineColumnSource: table byte a*9+9 in CHQ_unpacked.EXE at 0x341a0: attacker 1/2/3 -> next row col0 = 35, 4 -> 0, 5/6 -> 5, 7/8 -> 34, 9 -> 0x341fa = 25. A carrier as the target is therefore hit for 35 by infantry/tanks, 34 by subs/cruisers and 25 by another carrier; the table simply has no in-row column for kind 9.

rangeMatrix._comment: DS:0x1956, row = attacker range class, column = target class, values are SQUARED distance thresholds; column 5 is reused as the piece's own contact range. DS:0x194c maps kind to class: 0-4->0, 5-6->1, 7->2, 8->3, 9->4, 10-11->5.

That provenance clause sat in the player's sentence until PB-244 (frodo 9108 §7); it lives here now, where the next person reading `rosters` will find it.
notes.roundSeconds: 5 s chosen 2026-11-06 by the owner, and a DELIBERATE DEVIATION: the original's round is 119.5 s of game time and does not shorten with speed (measured 2026-11-12, T-008; see `measured` above and docs/re/MOVEMENT.md). At 1 cell per round the Washington-Moscow march is ~104 cells, about 8.7 minutes. The original felt like a campaign, not a 24-second war, and 0.14 s made income land every 3.5 s.

notes.prices: Manual p.28 lists these in billions. config stores the manual's billions; rules.priceOf() converts with money.perBillion and returns integer millions so no float drifts. The sub/cruiser/carrier row order comes from the p.28 icons and is UNVERIFIED until a DOSBox capture.

notes.captureReward: MEASURED, PB-155 (RE-E3). FUN_1c0d_02ce @ 1c0d:02ce: when a type-3 base or a type-4 city changes hands, the capturing side is paid 80 raw units (decompiled.c 9179-9182). The original's raw unit is 25 million (60000 units = 1500 b, the PB-151 clamp), so 80 raw = 2000 million = 2 b. DOSBox 2026-11-19 (docs/re/evidence/re3/, ECONOMY_RE.md section 3): three city captures, the flip sample being the post-capture 0.1 s sample: the CAPTURER stepped +80 units and the loser +0 at an unchanged round counter. A capital or an oil field pays nothing.

FUN_1c0d_02ce @ 1c0d:02ce writes 0x10ae[site] = 15 when a city or base changes hands (decompiled.c 9169): a flat 15-round timer on the captured site, independent of the pooled production formula. Read back in DOSBox on three captures (0 -> 15, and only that site's timer moved); it decays one per round.
notes.payingCount: Income is paid on the original's expression, not on the asset list's kind (PB-150): count(type 4) + max(0, count(type 1) + count(type 2) - 1). A base, an oil field, a dock and a world.json well carry no paying subtype. The old money.capitalPays flag is retired by this rule, which reproduces the flag's off behaviour and the extra-capital case in one place.

PB-153 labels every rule that reads it DERIVED and points here and at RE-E6; if RE-E6 refutes the derivation (a hover on site 64 naming something else, or a bombing not costing oil) the PB is reverted. The world.json wells are drawn only, labelled non-original, and are not placement sites, readiness neighbours, capture targets or income producers.

From Monitor Four on the running original (Manual p.27; renderer FUN_3711_16a8 @ 3711:16a8 divides DS:0x148e by 0x28 at 3711:16f3), captured per era in docs/captures/startmoney-<era>-blue-monitor4-own.png and written up in docs/re/START_MONEY.md. 1918 10, 1942 50, 1986 50, 2023 600. 9999 is UNVERIFIED (memory read only) and is a deliberate stand-in. Red has no capture of its own: red is given the Blue value on purpose (a recorded stand-in) rather than an invented number.
notes.handicap: OPPONENT'S STARTING MONEY (Manual p.17: 'For all scenarios, you are allowed to adjust the amount of money with which your opponent begins the game... a handicapping device'). It is the opponent's pool only, never the player's: 1942 proves it, where the player starts with 50b and the spinner default is 030 (30b). Per-era defaults are stored because they are not constant (010 in 1918, 030 in 1942). The spinner applies to EVERY era, 2023 included; 2023's default 600 is CAPTURED, not a stand-in (PB-265: docs/captures/startmoney-2023-blue-spinner-default.png reads 6/0/0, and the war room then reads DS:0x148e = 24000 on both sides). Range 0-999 step 1 is an UNVERIFIED inference from the three digit columns; wrap behaviour is unknown. 1986's default is captured too (PB-265); only the ???? default is a stand-in, labelled in sources.handicap.
notes.rosters: Manual p.16. 1918 has no air power, tanks or carriers; 1942 adds them; 1986 adds nukes, aid, satellites and intel. 2023 uses the 1986 set. 9999 is UNVERIFIED and uses the 1986 set.
notes.speeds: The seven slot lengths for speeds 0-6, in seconds per round. All seven numbers are the owner's playability ramp (speed 1 = the old 5 s round, speed 6 = a hundred rounds a minute) and are a DELIBERATE DEVIATION from the original, which was measured on 2026-11-12 to run one 119.5 s round at every speed 0-6 and to make speed 0 a full stop for pieces but not for the round clock (T-008, docs/re/MOVEMENT.md). Index 0 keeps the original's 'time does not pass' meaning for pieces. A room carries its own speed and either seat may change it; both seat views see the number.
notes.move: cellsPerRound is the number of cells a kind may enter in one round. STAND-IN, UNMEASURED: only the manual's orderings are binding (tank up to 2x infantry, p.9; sea faster than land and transports slightly slower than other ships, p.21). The walker's route test uses the archive's own DS:0x011C cost bytes, which are recovered, not tuned, and stay in rules.mjs.
notes.fuel: STAND-IN. The archive's fuel reserve and burn were never recovered: 10000 reserve and 1 per round are invented and are here only so a side can run short. Per side, deliberately not the desktop archive's single shared reserve.
notes.steel: STAND-IN, an owner-designed expansion and not a recovery: the 1990 game had oil only. 40 held and 1 a round are invented so a second kind can be held and consumed. No yield is set on purpose: the archive never recovered one, so the server refuses to hand out steel rather than guess a number. Gated to 1942 and 1986; the other scenarios do not carry it.
notes.combat: T-003 replaces the desktop archive's stand-in fight (after HITS shots the defender is gone) with the manual's strength model (p.20-25). Every key in `combat` carries its own source. A value marked STAND-IN, UNMEASURED is a working number the owner may replace, not a recovered one; the combat panel says 'unmeasured' for those. Damage removes a unit only when a hit meets or exceeds its remaining strength (p.23). Relatives the manual states are kept: tank > infantry, entrenched takes less, flank takes more, sub < cruiser < carrier range.
notes.air: The 8 and 4 are the booklet counts (docs/POLISH_LOOP.md: air mission inactive 8 rounds, scramble 4). The reach of 10 is a STAND-IN: the archive's aircraft range was not recovered. PB-178 splits the manual's two circles: air.restrictedReach 6 (UNVERIFIED port value) is the smaller radius a mission target must lie inside (manual p.25), while air.reach 10 stays the maximum radius the berth search and an unloaded transfer use. PB-188 gates STRIKE by the same circle as Bomb (port decision, UNVERIFIED; patrol keeps the open range as the defensive scramble).
notes.nukes: A nuke is refused by default. When config turns it on, a strike costs 10b, kills within nukes.killRadius (3, a PORT DECISION - the manual's three spaces, read as a square), paints wasteland on every land cell it covers, and leaves satellites alone; exclusion 2 is a STAND-IN home-ground ring the archive never printed, and a config that loses it now REFUSES rather than substituting. The after-effects (PB-233) are the manual's p.30 sentences: world opinion moves against every country the blast touched (the archive's shape, a STAND-IN magnitude), some of the attacked nation's cities switch, and a skipped payday says which cities the 5n gate took (the manual's 'production reduced by 25 per cent or more' is that gate - 5n per detonation IS 25 at the fifth - not a second cut: frodo 8983 §4). The launch rule is DECODED (PB-156): Manual p.30 plus FUN_1eb5_0eae's one global count at 0x148c - a side may lead by at most launchLead 3 launches, income is paid only on rnd(100) >= 5n (decompiled.c 4772), the warning comes from 5 detonations (12198) and nuclear winter (a loss for both) can end the war from 10 when rnd(100) < 100 / (20 - n) (12193). The 100% clamp at n >= 20 is an EXTRAPOLATION, not a decode: the original's 100 / (20 - n) is undefined there, so the block stops at a certain winter rather than guess. The numbers live in nukes.* above, each with its own ...Source; with enabled:false none of it runs.
notes.overrun: Overrun is the tank's (Manual p.9): an ordered tank that meets enemy infantry in the next cell fights through it, taking losses, and enters the cell and continues if the infantry is destroyed. There is no count-based instant removal. The losses are `combat.baseDamage` for both sides.
notes.placement: D-019, the original's rule (Manual p.27 'General Placement Rules'). Land units and aircraft may be placed on a friendly city or base cell; ships only on a friendly dock, so a side with no port cannot buy a hull. There is no reach any more: config carries no zone or coast number because the rule is a site kind, not a distance. The archive's validator could not be located in the Ghidra export (the strings 'Must be placed in city', 'Must be placed on dock', 'Must be on mainland', 'Friendly waters only', 'Ships must stay at sea.' exist in the extract's string dump, but the export has no string cross-references); FUN_107e_4140 was mislabelled in the old ECONOMY.md summary and is in fact the arrival/berth search (five-ring scan for a free cell of an acceptable terrain class), not the validator. A dock is DERIVED from the extract, not a recovered rule: board.matchSites builds one dock site on every terrain cell with id 1, and the world's own counts report 150 docks for 150 paint cells. 'A friendly dock is the dock next to a friendly site' is likewise derived from world.json (150 of 150 dock cells take the country of an adjacent site), not a measured original rule. See docs/re/PLACEMENT.md.
notes.readiness: DECODED, FUN_2dfc_1874 @ 2dfc:1874 (PB-154). Manual p.27 describes the shape; the archive gives the arithmetic: caps = 1 + the side's owned capitals (type 1/2) among records 0-63; the list is the build site plus every site of the side among records 0-63 with Euclidean d^2 < 401 (X wrapped at 320), with the build site counted twice; total = the listed sites' current remaining timers + floor(floor(price_b * 80 / 3) / caps); each listed site's remaining timer becomes floor(total / count), +1 when total % count > count / 2; timers drop by 1 per round. In the concealed era (9999) capitals are exempt for a side's first five builds via the per-side counter at 0x1580 (seat.bought). Peacetime is N/A: this build has no peace state, so every production tires its site. priceScaleNumerator/priceScaleDenominator carry 80/3 because JSON cannot hold the fraction exactly. Confirm-or-refute leg: RE-E2 (one DOSBox case) - if it disagrees, DOSBox wins and this block is reverted.

air.restrictedReachSource: UNVERIFIED PORT VALUE, PB-178. Manual p.25 names two circles: "the restricted air radius in which most missions must be performed" and the larger "maximum air radius", which an unloaded transfer may use. The archive's only air-range figure is the stand-in `reach`, recovered nowhere (see reachSource), so BOTH numbers here are the remake's: `restrictedReach` 6 is the smaller circle a MISSION's target must lie inside, `reach` 10 stays the maximum radius the berth search and an unloaded transfer use. Nothing in decompiled.c or the RE docs prints either size; PM files the DOSBox measurement, and when it lands these two keys are corrected, not the rule. PB-188 (PORT DECISION, UNVERIFIED, ruling in room 8383 §4): the circle is a property of the AIR LAYER, so a STRIKE is gated by it exactly like a bombing run - the manual's sentence says "most missions", and leaving a strike at reach 10 while a bomb may not fly 7 would make the circle a property of one order button. PATROL keeps the open range: it is the defensive scramble and already defaults to the aircraft's own cell, so gating it would stack a second unverified assumption on the unverified 6. If the DOSBox measurement shows the original tested every mission's target distance, patrol joins then.
air.transferRoundsSource: UNVERIFIED. Manual printed p.22 names only the sites an air unit may transfer to (cities, bases, carriers); it prints no round cost for a transfer and no read site that charges one was recovered in decompiled.c. 0 is the remake's assumption (a transfer rebases the aircraft, it is not a mission), recorded as Q50's sub-item. Nothing outside this file treats it as recovered.

air.reachSource: STAND-IN, UNMEASURED. The aircraft range was never recovered: manual p.22 prints no number and no read site was found. `reach` gates strikes, the mission base search and the transfer range alike, and every refusal that names it calls it a stand-in.
air.bombSource: DECODED, PB-157. FUN_1ac5_0dbe @ 1ac5:0dbe, decompiled.c 8768-8782; MANUAL p.25. An air mission on an unoccupied enemy city or base takes 5 of the original's money units from the owner and adds 5 to the site's timer. The original's panel divides cash by 40 (START_MONEY.md), so 5 units = 125 M; this port stores cash in millions (money.perBillion 1000), so the charge is 125. A type-5 oil field is the oil branch: the owner's next-round oil available drops by 1000 raw units (8 on the panel's /125 scale). The mission costs the same 8 rounds as a strike and shares its resolution path; the original's own strike handler is the one measured, not a second roll invented here.

PB-158 moves the reveal itself to the server: an enemy piece is in the scanner's payload only while the bar's server-side span covers its column. nukes.exclusionSource: STAND-IN (PB-230; made fail-closed in PB-233). Manual p.30 names a capital guard but never prints its size. The ring is config, so a config that loses this key REFUSES a launch (NUKE_EXCLUSION_UNKNOWN, web/server/nukestrike.mjs) instead of falling back to the literal 2 it used to substitute - frodo's M9 on the PB-229/230 gate, ruled into PB-233.
nukes.killRadiusSource: PORT DECISION, UNVERIFIED (PB-230). Manual p.30: the kill zone destroys 'everything within three spaces' of ground zero, land, sea and air units, cities, bases and oil fields, both sides'. The 3 is the manual's own count, read as CHEBYSHEV distance (a square) because every other radius in this build is a square - capital exclusion and the satellite scan. No decode and no DOSBox leg has pinned the shape or the count; web/server/nukestrike.mjs says STAND-IN in every event it emits.
nukes.attitudeShiftSource: DECODED SHAPE, STAND-IN magnitude (PB-233). Ghidra FUN_1eb5_0eae, decompiled.c 12133-12166: a signed attitude byte per nation at 0x13e4 is moved by (0x13be[nation] & 0xf) * one global sign, halved when that magnitude is no bigger than the referenced attitude byte (local_8 & 0x3f, not resolved by the export), nudged by 1 when the halved value is 0 and the gate byte is odd, then clamped to +-0x7f. web/server/aftermath.mjs ports the halving, the odd nudge and the clamp exactly. The per-nation nibble table (1..15) does not exist in this build, so 4 is a STAND-IN drawn from that range.
nukes.switchChanceSource: STAND-IN (PB-233). Manual p.30: 'The number of cities that switch is partly random' - the manual names no chance. 50 per cent, one rnd(100) in web/server/aftermath.mjs, taken off a SECOND seeded stream so a launch cannot move PB-156's decoded draw order (launch roll, then the two paydays).
nukes.switchPerCitySource: STAND-IN (PB-233). Manual p.30: 'partly determined by civilian casualties (represented by destruction of cities)'. The manual names the term and no rate: 1 city switches per city the strike levelled. The archive's owner flip at decompiled.c 12167-12185 walks 100 PIECE slots, so it yields no city count to decode.
nukes.switchPerLossSource: STAND-IN (PB-233). Manual p.30: 'and friendly casualties caused by the nuke'. A term with no rate: 1 city switches per unit of the FIRER's own that died in the blast.
nukes.firstStrikePenaltySource: STAND-IN (PB-233). Manual p.30: 'Also, the first side to use nukes suffers an additional penalty in this regard.' The penalty is never quantified: 2 extra cities, applied only when the firer has fired once and the other side has not fired at all (web/server/aftermath.mjs isFirstFirer, read off the same counters as the lead rule).
nukes.source: DECODED, PB-156. Manual p.30: at most 3 more nukes than the opponent has fired, so launchLead is the DIFFERENCE of the two counters (fired(mine) - fired(theirs) < 3), not one side's total. FUN_1eb5_0eae increments one global count at 0x148c (decompiled.c 12036-12039): from 5 the original warns (sprite drawn when 4 < count, 12198-12199), from 10 nuclear winter if rnd(100) < 100 / (20 - n) (winterDivisor 20, decompiled.c 12193-12197), and each round income is paid only if rnd(100) >= 5n (incomeSkipPerDetonation 5, decompiled.c 4772 - the gate is the 0x148c*5 <= 0x1488 test, NOT 4763, which writes a city's income into 0x144e). The roll is the match's own seeded stream (web/server/rng.mjs), so a reload replays the same round. The 100% clamp at n >= 20 is an EXTRAPOLATION, not a decode: the original divides 100 by (20 - n), which has no defined value at 20 and no sensible one above it, so this block stops at a certain winter instead of inventing the original's undefined branch. `enabled:false` keeps the whole block inert, as shipped. The after-effects of a strike (PB-233: attitude and the city switch) carry their own ...Source siblings above; every numeric key here must resolve one, and web/test/nodes/pb233_sources.mjs fails the suite if one does not. The manual's third sentence, 'All city production is reduced by 25 per cent or more', is NOT ported as arithmetic: there is no production multiply in FUN_1eb5_0eae, and 5n per detonation IS 25 per cent at the fifth detonation, so the gate above is that sentence and its growth. Frodo ruled the flat cut out on 2026-11-24 (room 8983 §4); what PB-233 ships is legibility - economy.pay's skipped payday names the cities whose payday the gate took.

blast.source: PB-231. Manual L343-345 + p.29 for the killer satellite: pick a destination, start over the home capital, travel fast, detonate on arrival, kill every satellite of BOTH sides within about six cells, retarget when the target moves. The count is NOT recovered - the booklet says 'about six' and the extract carries only the KILLSAT/BLOWSAT/SPYSAT animations - so radius 6 is a STAND-IN and web/server/blast.mjs says so in every event it emits. peace._comment: PB-245 / T-035. Manual printed p.31-32: 'Peace lasts for a pre-set amount of time, depending upon the scenario. A counter in Monitor One tells you how much time remains in mandatory peace' and 'Cash, however, still accumulates, and at an accelerated rate.' The page prints NO length and NO rate. mandatoryRounds is keyed by scenario; an absent key means the page printed no mandatory window for that scenario, not that the window is zero rounds. PAID PER TICK, NOT MULTIPLIED (T-035, RE-E4 capture A): the cold war runs NO round (0x1476 stayed 0 for 150 s) and pays a flat 10 original cash units twice a second from FUN_15f4_0cdc, so this block carries the per-tick amount and the tick rate instead of a multiplier over wartime income. The 0x148e cash field is in 40ths of a billion (docs/re/ECONOMY_RE.md:163), and money.perBillion is 1000, so 10 units x 1000/40 = 250 port money units per tick; two ticks a second reproduces the capture's +20 units/s (2170 -> 5110 over 149 s).
